input.body:
label: bug
file: src/ingest/parser.ts

The parser splits the file content with `text.split("\n")` only, so it doesn't account for Windows-style CRLF line endings. When a file uses `\r\n`, the trailing `\r` remains attached to the last field of each line, which throws off the column count comparison against the header and triggers `errors.rowShape` ("Malformed row"). Since finance switched to a new Windows-based export tool, their files likely now use CRLF endings, explaining why every upload fails at row 1. The fix should normalize/strip `\r` characters (e.g. split on `/\r?\n/` or strip `\r` from each line) before validating column counts.

text: Found it: parser.ts splits on `"\n"` only, so Windows CRLF line endings (`\r\n`) leave a trailing `\r` on each field, causing column count mismatches reported at row 1. This matches the new Windows export tool.
